abstract.title: Abstract
abstract.p: Candida albicans is a common opportunistic pathogen, causing infections ranging from superficial to bloodstream infections. The limited antifungal options and rising drug resistance challenge clinical treatment. We screened 98 essential oils and identified 48 with antifungal activity against Candida albicans at 1% concentration, determining their minimum inhibitory concentrations (MIC). Of these, 14 maintained fungicidal activity at lower concentrations (0.25% and 0.125%). 5 essential oils (Cinnamon, Satureja montana, Palmarosa, Lemon eucalyptus, and Honey myrtle) showed the highest inhibitory effects on stationary-phase Candida albicans and inhibited hyphae elongation. Synergistic effects were observed when combining Palmarosa with amphotericin B (AmB) against growing-phase Candida albicans, while Cinnamon and Satureja montana with AmB showed superior efficacy against stationary-phase infections. We identified the active components of 5 essential oils using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) and found the following main constituents: Cinnamon primarily contains benzyl benzoate and eugenol, Satureja montana is dominated by carvacrol and cymene, Palmarosa features geraniol and geranyl acetate, Lemon eucalyptus includes dl-Isopulegol and citronellal, and Honey myrtle is characterized by citral and neral. Our results may aid in developing more effective antifungal treatments.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Invasive Candida infections are widely recognized as a major cause of morbidity and mortality in healthcare settings1, with Candida albicans being the primary pathogen responsible for candidemia, exhibiting mortality rates of up to 40%2. Candida albicans naturally colonizes the oral cavity, skin, gastrointestinal tract, and vagina3, but in individuals with immunodeficiency, dysbiosis, or environmental changes, its overgrowth can lead to severe symptoms, contributing to approximately 1.5 million deaths annually4,5. Effective antifungal treatment remains critical, yet the limited drug repertoire6 and growing resistance to azoles, echinocandins, and other antifungal agents present significant challenges7.

Emerging research highlights the potential of alternative therapies, including probiotics, photodynamic inactivation, bacteriophages, and phytomedicine8–11. Essential oils, obtained from plant materials through appropriate mechanical processes, have been shown to have bactericidal activity against Gram-negative bacteria, Gram-positive bacteria, and fungi such as Candida albicans and Aspergillus12,13. However, previous studies have largely focused on a limited range of essential oils and their effects on actively growing Candida14–16. The need for antifungal drugs is far from being met, and further research is needed to understand the impact of essential oils on the growth and viability of Candida albicans, in order to provide more effective antifungal agents.

In this study, we conducted antimicrobial activity screening of a large collection of 98 essential oils against stationary phase Candida albicans. Subsequently, the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) was determined to further identify the essential oils with lower MIC at 0.25% and 0.125%. Five essential oils, Cinnamon, Satureja montana, Palmarosa, Lemon eucalyptus, Honey myrtle, with best inhibitory effects were identified and their main active components were characterized. These essential oils were also selected to assess their combined antimicrobial effects with AmB and on the hyphae formation of Candida albicans, with the aim to provide new treatment strategies for Candida infections.

sec.title: Preliminary screening and MIC of antifungal active essential oils
sec.p: In the preliminary screening of 98 essential oils tested by 96-pin replicator, 48 essential oils were found to have antifungal activity against stationary phase Candida albicans at 1% final concentration. The MICs of these 48 essential oils and AmB included as a control drug were determined by microbroth dilution method (Table 1). Cinnamon essential oil had the strongest antifungal activity with MIC ≤ 0.0078%, followed by Palmarosa (MIC = 0.03125-0.125%), Satureja montana (MIC = 0.0625–0.125%), Siberian fir (MIC = 0.0625-0.25%), Peppermint (MIC = 0.0625-0.25%), Mandarin (MIC = 0.0625-0.25%). In addition, Candida albicans CMCC98001 was found to be sensitive to AmB with an MIC range of 0.25–0.5 µg/mL.

caption.p: MICs of 48 essential oils with antifungal activity against stationary phase Candida albicans at 1% final concentration.

sec.title: Antifungal effect of active essential oils on stationary phase Candida albicans
Evaluation of the antifungal effect of the active essential oils on stationary phase Candida albicans
sec.p: The fungicidal effect of the 48 active essential oils on stationary phase Candida albicans was evaluated by 96-pin replicator. The results revealed that 14 essential oils, Cinnamon, Satureja montana, Palmarosa, Thyme, Basil, Lemongrass, Verbena spanish, Honey myrtle, Peppermint, Marjoram, Rosewood, Lemon eucalyptus, Valerian, Vanilla, exhibited strong antifungal effects (Table 2). At the final concentration of 0.5%, almost all essential oils could completely kill the fungus on day 1, except Vanilla, which completely killed the fungus on day 3. At final concentrations of 0.25% and 0.125%, Cinnamon, Satureja montana and Palmarosa completely killed the fungus on the first day, while the other 11 essential oils could not completely kill the fungus, indicating that the three essential oils had the strongest fungicidal effect.

caption.p: Activity of selected active essential oils effective against stationary Candida albicans at different concentrations.

sec.title: Time-kill curve experiments to further evaluate essential oil activity on stationary phase Candida albicans
sec.p: To further study the antifungal effects of the aforementioned 14 essential oils, we performed the time-killing curve experiments with stationary phase Candida albicans (Fig. 1). The results indicated that at 0.25%, Palmarosa, Cinnamon, Satureja montana, Honey myrtle, Lemon eucalyptus, and Rosewood, completely eradicated stationary phase Candida albicans on the first day. Lemongrass, Thyme and Verbena spanish completely eradicated the fungus on the third day, while Basil and Marjoram achieved complete eradication on the fifth day. At a lower concentration of 0.125%, 5 essential oils had best effects, among which Palmarosa, Cinnamon, and Satureja montana completely killed Candida albicans on the first day, Lemon eucalyptus, Honey myrtle completely killed on day 3. The results were consistent with the preliminary evaluation, suggesting that Cinnamon, Satureja montana and Palmarosa were more effective in killing stationary phase Candida albicans, followed by Lemon eucalyptus and Honey myrtle.

caption.p: Time-kill curve of 14 essential oils against stationary phase Candida albicans. (A) The time-kill curve of essential oils at 0.25%. Palmarosa, Cinnamon, Satureja montana, Honey myrtle, Lemon eucalyptus, and Rosewood, completely eradicated stationary phase Candida albicans on the first day. (B) The time-kill curve of essential oils at 0.125%. Palmarosa, Cinnamon, and Satureja montana completely killed Candida albicans on the first day, and Honey myrtle and Lemon eucalyptus killed all fungi at 3 days. All essential oil groups were significantly different from drug-free control group. P<0.0001(ANOVA).

sec.title: Effects of essential oils on the hyphae formation of Candida albicans
sec.p: The effect of the five best-performing essential oils against stationary phase Candida albicans essential oils on the hyphae morphology was determined by fluorescent microscopy. As shown in Fig. 2, all the 5 essential oils Cinnamon, Satureja montana, Palmarosa, Lemon eucalyptus and Honey myrtle affected the hyphae formation. The results showed that untreated Candida albicans formed bud tubes within 2 h and long hyphae within 6 h, with no apparent fungal cell death. In contrast, the length of hyphae of Candida albicans treated with 0.03125% above-mentioned five essential oils was obviously shortened (Fig. 2), indicating an inhibitory effect on hyphae formation. Among them, Cinnamon, Satureja montana, and Palmarosa had the most obvious inhibitory effects, with a higher level of cell death observed at 6 h compared to the other groups.

caption.p: Inhibitory effect of essential oils on the hyphae formation of Candida albicans. In the control group, budding spores were observed at 2 h, and hyphae appeared at 6 h. The growth of Candida albicans hyphae was inhibited at 0.03125% of the 5 most active essential oils. Green fluorescence represents the dead cells stained with SYTOX Green in the field of view. Cinnamon, Satureja montana, and Palmarosa essential oils killed more fungi. BF (Bright field), FL (Fluorescent light).

sec.title: Effect of essential oil combination with antifungal drugs
FICI determination
sec.p: FICI values of the 5 most active essential oils combined with AmB were determined by checkerboard dilution method, and the interaction between the two agents was determined based on the results (Fig. 3). The results showed that the FICI values were as follows: Lemon eucalyptus FICI = 0.750, Cinnamon FICI = 0.750, Honey myrtle FICI = 0.516, Satureja montana FICI = 0.625, and Palmarosa FICI = 0.375. It can be concluded that Palmarosa essential oil had a synergistic effect with AmB, while the others had an additive effect.

caption.p: FICI determination of the 5 most active essential oils combined with AmB. Each square represents a well filled with Candida albicans suspension and different concentrations of essential oils and AmB. In the red area, the suspension is cloudy, and in the blue area, it is clear. Minimum FICI values are indicated in the picture. Cinnamon FICI = 0.750, Lemon eucalyptus FICI = 0.750, Satureja montana FICI = 0.625, Honey myrtle FICI = 0.516, and Palmarosa FICI = 0.375.

sec.title: Time-kill curve experiments of essential oils combined with AmB on stationary phase Candida albicans
sec.p: In time-kill experiments, it was observed that on the first day of combined drug treatment of Candida albicans, Satureja montana + AmB and Palmarosa + AmB exhibited the fastest decrease in colony count. Starting from the third day, the fungicidal effect of AmB, Lemon eucalyptus + AmB, Honey myrtle + AmB, and Palmarosa + AmB decreased, leading to an increase in fungal load. Ultimately, the drug combinations Satureja montana + AmB and Cinnamon + AmB completely killed Candida albicans on the third and fifth day, respectively, while individual essential oils or drug alone were unable to achieve complete eradication (Fig. 4).

caption.p: Time-kill curve of the most active essential oils combined with AmB on stationary phase Candida albicans. The final concentration is 2 µg/mL for AmB and 0.03125% for essential oils. The drug combinations Satureja montana + AmB and Cinnamon + AmB completely killed Candida albicans on the third and fifth day, respectively, whereas each singly alone could not.

sec.title: Determination of the composition of the 5 most effective essential oils
sec.p: By assessing the antifungal activity of essential oils against Candida albicans, we identified five essential oils with notable efficacy: Cinnamon, Satureja montana, Palmarosa, Lemon eucalyptus, and Honey myrtle. Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) analysis revealed their active components (Table 3): Cinnamon oil comprises benzyl benzoate, eugenol, linalool, and trans-Cinnamaldehyde; Satureja montana is based on the phenolic compound carvacrol, as well as o-cymene, gamma-terpinene and other ingredients; Palmarosa oil features monoterpenes such as geraniol, geranyl acetate, and linalool; Lemon eucalyptus contains citronellal, dl-Isopulegol, and citronellol, among which citronellal has the highest peak area and concentration; Honey myrtle oil is primarily composed of citral, neral, and geraniol. Total ion chromatograms and key molecular structures are illustrated in Fig. 5.

caption.p: The GC-MS result of the five most active essential oils.
GC-MS total ion chromatograms (TICs) of the 5 most active essential oils. The TICs of Cinnamon, Satureja montana, Palmarosa, Lemon eucalyptus, and Honey Myrtle are presented.

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: Candida albicans is one of the main causes for hospital-acquired infections, which is particularly severe in immunocompromised individuals17,18. Currently, the drugs used to treat Candida infections are limited and the widespread and long-term use of antifungal drugs has led to increasing resistance, particularly to azoles and echinocandins5,7. This growing resistance, coupled with the scarcity of effective antifungal agents, underscores the critical need for new therapeutic strategies. Here, we screened 98 essential oils for antifungal activity against Candida albicans and identified 5 most active essential oils (Cinnamon, Satureja montana, Palmarosa, Lemon eucalyptus, Honey myrtle). Additionally, we found that the combination of Palmarosa and AmB had a synergistic killing effect on growing phase Candida albicans and that the combined application of Cinnamon and Satureja montana with AmB respectively had better efficacy against stationary phase Candida albicans than AmB or single essential oil alone.

Essential oil is a secondary metabolite extracted from plants such as myrtaceae, rutaceae, Compositaceae and labiaceae19. In recent years, essential oils have received attention in novel antimicrobial development in face of increasing antibiotic resistant microbial infections. In our previous research, it was found that 0.032% (v/v) essential oils of oregano, cinnamon bark, and others could eradicate stationary phase Bartonella henselae20. Oregano oil, in combination with tosufloxacin and rifampin, completely eliminated stationary phase S. aureus21. There have also been some studies on the antifungal effects of essential oils. However, so far only a small number of essential oils have been reported to have antifungal activity against Candida albicans. For example, oregano oil has been shown to inhibit Candida biofilm formation22, Lavender essential oil exhibited activity against Candida albicans23. In our study, we evaluated a large panel of 98 essential oils and found 48 essential oils which exhibited antifungal activity. Among them, Siberian fir, Galbanum, Amber oil, Silver fir, Dill herb, Bay sweet tree, Honey myrtle, and Ravintsara essential oil have not been reported for their antifungal activity against Candida albicans. We also found that Cinnamon essential oil had the lowest MIC, followed by Palmarosa, Satureja montana, Siberian fir, Peppermint and Mandarin. We conducted further assessments of the fungicidal effects and found that Cinnamon, Satureja montana, and Palmarosa demonstrated the strongest fungicidal effects on the stationary phase Candida albicans, being able to completely eradicate the yeast on the first day even at lower concentrations of 0.25% and 0.125%, followed by Lemon eucalyptus, and Honey myrtle.

The yeast cells of Candida albicans are spherical to oval, while the hyphae cells are tubular24. The transition from yeast form to hyphae form plays a central role in the pathogenesis of Candida albicans. Hyphae is naturally invasive, able to penetrate the epithelial and endothelial barriers of the host, and can also express degrading enzymes, cell surface adhesins, pore-forming toxins and other virulence factors25. It has been found that Ocimum sanctum essential oil26, the components camphor and fenchone derivatives in Cedar leaf essential oil27, can inhibit the morphological transition of Candida albicans from yeast to hyphae form by suppressing hyphae-specific and biofilm-related genes. In our study, the five essential oils that exhibited the strongest fungicidal effects on stationary phase Candida albicans were able to inhibit hyphae formation at a low concentration of 0.03125%. Among them, Palmarosa, Satureja montana, and Cinnamon showed the most significant inhibitory effects on germ tube formation and hyphae elongation. This finding could indicate their potential to effectively combat hyphae formation of Candida albicans and may reduce the invasion of host tissues by the fungus and the progression of the disease.

The interaction between plant extracts and antibiotics has attracted widespread attention. Amphotericin B (AmB) is a widely used drug for treating invasive fungal infections28. However, its use is limited by renal toxicity and hemolytic potential. Combining antifungal drugs with other agents can enhance efficacy, reduce dosages, and combat drug resistance. In this study, we found that Palmarosa essential oil combined with AmB exhibited a synergistic effect against Candida albicans in the FICI test. Additionally, time-kill assays revealed that Cinnamon and Satureja montana essential oils combined with AmB provided superior therapeutic effects on stationary-phase Candida albicans compared to single agents. Considering the above results, we will further investigate the fungicidal efficacy and safety of the active essential oils combined with AmB in animal models.

GC-MS analysis of the five most effective essential oils (Cinnamon, Satureja montana, Palmarosa, Lemon eucalyptus, and Honey myrtle) identified their main components as eugenol, carvacrol, geraniol, citronellal, and citral, respectively. These compounds are widely used as flavorings and fragrances in food and cosmetics. For instance, eugenol disrupts Gram-negative bacterial membrane29, while carvacrol and geraniol exhibit antioxidant, antibacterial, and anti-inflammatory properties30,31. Citral plays a role in inflammation regulation through inhibition of NF-κB and JNK/p38 pathways32. The inhibitory effects of these active components on Candida albicans and their fungicidal mechanisms should be further studied to maximize their potential applications and aid in the clinical treatment of candidiasis.

sec.title: Conclusion
sec.p: In summary, we performed a large-scale screening of 98 essential oils and identified Cinnamon, Satureja montana, Palmarosa, Lemon eucalyptus, and Honey myrtle as the five most active essential oils that exhibited good antifungal activity against both growing form and stationary phase non-growing Candida albicans, as well as inhibited hyphae formation. Palmarosa in combination with AmB demonstrated synergistic effects against growing phase Candida albicans, while the combination of Cinnamon and Satureja montana with AmB showed better treatment effects against stationary phase Candida albicans compared to individual agents. The main components of the five most active essential oils identified were Eugenol, Carvacrol, Geraniol, Citronellal, and Citral. These findings may offer new opportunity for improved treatment of Candida albicans infections in the future.

sec.title: Essential oils and antifungal drugs
sec.p: In this study, we screened 98 essential oils purchased from different online vendors including Ningbo Glantu Electronic Industry and Trade Co., Ltd (Ningbo, China), Guangzhou La Gu Na Biotechnology Co., Ltd (Guangzhou, China), Poli Aromatic Pharmaceutical Technology Co., Ltd (Shanghai, China), Plant Therapy (USA), Healing solutions (USA) and Prime Time Commerce (Scottsdale Arizona, USA). For the specific list, see Supplementary Table S1. The essential oils were stored at 4℃ and diluted with DMSO to 20% concentration at 1:4 ratio before use33. The control group was diluted by the same method as the essential oil, with a mixture of 80% DMSO and 20% PBS (4:1). In our preliminary study, we found Candida albicans can tolerate up to 5% DMSO. The DMSO concentrations used in our experiments were less than 4% to ensure DMSO does not have direct antimycotic effect. The Amphotericin B (Cas 1397-89-3) was purchased from Shanghai Yuanye Biotechnology Company and was prepared in DMSO as a stock solution of 2560 µg/ml, which was then stored at -20℃.

sec.title: Fungal strain and culture conditions
sec.p: The strain used in this study was Candida albicans (CMCC 98001), which was obtained from China General Microbiological Culture Collection Center. Candida albicans was inoculated with Sabouraud Dextrose Agar (SDA, cas S9710, Solarbio) after recovery. After overnight cultivation, single colonies were selected and inoculated in YPD broth (cas LA0250, Solarbio), and incubated at 37℃ with shaking at 200 rpm for 24 h to obtain the stationary phase Candida albicans.

sec.title: Screening of antifungal activity of 98 essential oils
sec.p: The 96-pin replicator can rapidly replicate samples for biological experiments by transferring small volumes of samples from the mother plate to the daughter plate21.

When conducting the preliminary screening of antifungal activity for 98 essential oils, the essential oils were diluted to a final concentration of 1% in a 96-well plate and then added to stationary phase Candida albicans. On the 7th day, a 96-pin replicator was used to transfer the content from the 96-well plate to SDA agar plates. For the further determination of the fungicidal effect of different concentration (0.5%, 0.25%, 0.125%) essential oils on stationary phase Candida, the mixture was transferred to SDA agar plates on the 1st, 3rd and 5th day of essential oil exposure, respectively. After 24 h of cultivation, the presence or absence of colony growth at the corresponding positions on plates was observed and recorded for antifungal activity.‘-’ indicates no obvious colony growth, while ‘+’ indicates obvious colony growth.

sec.title: Determination of minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC)
sec.p: In accordance with the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) Guidelines (CLSI M27-A3), the MIC of essential oils with antifungal activity was measured using microdilution method in a 96-well U-shaped bottom microtitration plate. Adjust the Candida albicans cells to 0.5 McFarland (approximately 1 × 106 to 5 × 106 CFU/mL), and dilute with RPMI 1640 medium at a ratio of 1:1000. The essential oils were 2-fold diluted from 1 to 0.0078%. AmB concentration ranged from 16 µg/ml to 0.125 µg/ml. The 96-well cell culture plates were placed in a constant temperature incubator at 37℃ for 48 h.

sec.title: Time-kill assay
sec.p: The time-kill curve of essential oils against Candida albicans was determined. Candida albicans in stationary phase (approximately 108 CFU/mL) was used as the initial inoculum. Candida albicans was incubated with essential oils at concentrations of 0.25% and 0.125% (v/v) respectively, and the killing ability was measured at days 0, 1, 3, 5 and 7. At each time point, 100 µl fungal suspension was taken and 10-fold diluted, and 10µL of the diluted suspension was plated for CFU counting on SDA plates.

sec.title: Germ tube and hyphae inhibition experiment
sec.p: Candida albicans single colonies with a diameter greater than 1 mm were selected and cultured in YPD medium at 30 °C with shaking at 200 rpm for 48 h to obtain synchronized fungal spores34. The Candida albicans culture was diluted to 0.5 McFarland in RPMI-1640 medium containing 10% fetal bovine serum (for hyphae culture). Then, 1 ml of the diluted fungal culture was mixed with essential oils at final concentrations of 0.03125% in a 6-well plate and incubated at 37 °C. SYTOX Green (a dead cell nucleic acid dye) was added at 1.5 h and 5.5 h, followed by a 30-minute incubation period, after which the fungal germination was observed under an inverted fluorescence microscope (Olympus IX73) and photographed at 2 h and 6 h.

sec.title: FICI determination
sec.p: Broth checkerboard method was used to test the combination of essential oils and AmB. Essential oils and AmB were diluted sequentially in a 96-well microtiter plate. AmB was 2-fold diluted along the vertical axis from the concentration of 2 µg/ml, and essential oils were diluted from the concentration of 1% along the horizontal axis. Candida albicans was adjusted to 0.5 McFarland, and then diluted in RPMI 1640 medium at a ratio of 1:1000 before adding to each well. Then, 96-well plates were cultured at 37℃ for 24–48 h. The Fractional Inhibitory Concentration Index (FICI) for the combined drugs was calculated using the following formula:
The interpretation criteria for the results were as follows: FICI ≤ 0.5 indicates synergy; 0.5 < FICI ≤ 1 indicates addition; 1 < FICI ≤ 4 indicates no interaction; and FICI>4 indicates antagonism35.

sec.title: Determination of combined antifungal effect of essential oils and AmB by killing curve experiments
sec.p: Candida albicans was cultured to stationary phase with a concentration of approximately 108 CFU/mL. The combined application of essential oils and AmB was used, at a final concentration of 2 µg/mL for AmB and 0.03125% for essential oils. The killing ability of the drug combination against stationary phase Candida albicans was measured at day 0, 1, 3, 5 and 7. At each time point, 200µL of the above mixture was serially diluted tenfold, and CFU counts were performed on SDA plates. Results were recorded after 24 h of incubation at 37 °C.

sec.title: GC-MS analyses
sec.p: The chemical components of essential oils were analyzed using an Agilent 7890B/5977A mass spectrometer. The GC column was DB-5MS (30 m × 0.25 mm × 0.25 μm). The initial column temperature set at 50 °C, which was then increased at a rate of 2 °C/min to 260 °C after 2 min. The injector temperature was 260 °C, and the detector temperature was 280 °C. Helium was used as the carrier gas at a flow rate of 1.37 mL/min. All samples were diluted to a 1:10 ratio in dichloromethane (DCM) and injected at a split ratio of 1:30 with a volume of 0.3 µL. Mass scanning was set to collect data in the range of 35 to 650 m/z. Qualitative analysis of the GC/MS data was performed using Agilent MassHunter Workstation software.

sec.title: Data analysis
sec.p: The data was analyzed and plotted using GraphPad Prism (version 7.0). The data provided were the mean plus or minus standard deviations of three independent experiments. To evaluate statistical significance, two-way ANOVA test and Dunnett’s multiple comparison test were used for comparisons between groups at different time points, and the results were significant when p value was ≤ 0.05.
